title: Processing of identified data during parent registration
description: The Authentication Service explicitly requests and processes identified personal data including email, name, and government ID from the parent user during registration.
assumptions: The registration flow requires these specific data elements as stated in the flow description.

title: Unique identifiers in registration data
description: Email address and government ID serve as unique references to the identity of the parent user, enabling direct identification.
assumptions: Email and government ID are unique identifiers for the data subject.

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The email, government ID, and six-digit code can be used to link this parent's data across different systems or within the authentication service over time.
assumptions: These identifiers are stored and potentially used for cross-referencing.

title: Collection of highly sensitive government ID data
description: Government ID is a highly sensitive data type. Its collection during parent registration may exceed what is functionally required for authentication purposes.
assumptions: Government ID is more sensitive than typical authentication credentials like email/password.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if govt ID is strictly necessary for this authentication context - depends on specific use case requirements.

title: Excessive amount of personal data collected
description: Multiple data points are collected (email, password, name, government ID, six-digit code) which may exceed the minimum necessary for parent registration and authentication.
assumptions: All five data elements are collected in a single registration flow.

title: Attributable registration data
description: The registration data can be used to attribute the parent user's actions and prevent them from denying their registration or subsequent authentication activities.
assumptions: Registration data is stored and linked to user actions.

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: The parent user may not be fully aware of how their registration data (especially government ID) will be processed, stored, or shared beyond the initial authentication purpose.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all processing activities.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the quality of privacy notices provided during registration.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting government ID and multiple data points may violate GDPR's data minimization principle if all data is not strictly necessary for the authentication functionality.
assumptions: GDPR or similar privacy regulations apply to this system.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether govt ID is legally required or functionally necessary for this specific authentication context.
